signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Surrender
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5856 trades with heavy selling pressure after the RBNZ delivered a 25bp hike to 2.75% but paired it with a signal for gradual tightening. The RBNZ's explicit goal to reduce the risk of larger future hikes has triggered a sharp repricing, sending NZD to the bottom of the G10 scorecard with a -1.097% weekly average. Technicals show the pair has lost the SMA20 at 0.5912, now testing the SMA200 at 0.5852. COT positioning was already extremely crowded short with an LF net of -32,496 (0th percentile), but the lack of a hawkish surprise has forced a capitulation of the recovery thesis. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; gradual tightening signal removes the floor for the currency. Catalyst: next high-impact US data release. Risk: a sharp recovery in global risk sentiment that lifts commodity-linked pairs despite policy divergence.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Options Complementarity
signals.text: USD/JPY at 160.27 remains bid above the psychologically critical 160.00 level which has historically prompted MoF verbal warnings. Despite the 270bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage supporting the pair, institutional options data reveals significant defensive positioning with a 25d Risk Reversal of -1.79. This strong put skew indicates that while spot remains elevated, market participants are paying a high premium for downside protection against a potential intervention or BoJ surprise. The JPY ESI at +27.9 supports a fundamental case for JPY strength that speculators have yet to embrace, with LF net remaining short at -81,619. Trade bias: Neutral/Caution USD/JPY; spot at 160+ triggers acute intervention risk despite carry support. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting on 18 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: BoJ holds with no hawkish shift, allowing carry-seekers to push the pair toward 162.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Macro Data + Retail-Positioning Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7145 is holding above its SMA20 at 0.7114 following a Q2 GDP beat of 0.4%, which keeps a September RBA holds at 4.35%. This fundamental strength contrasts with extreme retail sentiment where 84% of community traders are short, attempting to fade the recent recovery. COT data confirms institutional support with LF net long at +53,578 (95th percentile), creating a clear divergence where retail is fighting the institutional trend and the supportive data backdrop. While the 60bp carry disadvantage vs USD remains a structural headwind, the data-driven support for the RBA's 4.35% rate provides a floor. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; supported by GDP beat and institutional-retail divergence. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold priced. Risk: a broader USD rally driven by US 10Y yield surges above 4.85%.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3508 is currently trading below its SMA20 at 1.3549 but maintains a mildly restrictive real rate of +0.35%. The most notable feature in the pair is the extreme volatility risk premium, with implied volatility at 11.0% vs a realized 30-day volatility of only 4.9%. This 6.1-point VRP suggests the options market is pricing in significant event risk or a regime shift that has not yet manifested in spot price action. Given that COT positioning for GBP is crowded long at +56,839 (96th percentile), the high cost of protection suggests institutional fear of a positioning unwind. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; extreme VRP makes long exposure expensive relative to realized moves. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: a sudden shift in UK inflation data that forces a repricing of the 3.75% BoE hold bias.
